entry.title: feat: add forgetCards and setDueDate scheduling tools (#60)
entry.content:
feat: add forgetCards and setDueDate scheduling tools (#60)

* feat: add forgetCards and setDueDate scheduling tools

Both tools change a card's schedule without recording a review, which is
what separates them from rate_card. Until now the only way to push a card
back into rotation was rate_card with a rating of 1 — that logs a real
review, counts as a lapse and drops the card's ease factor, permanently
skewing future scheduling and review statistics.

forgetCards resets cards to the new queue and reports each card's prior
state (previousState, previousIntervalDays, reps, lapses) so callers can
show what was given up. setDueDate moves the next review by N days using
Anki's spec format ("0", "3-7", "1!"), keeping interval and ease, and
reads the scheduling back so range specs report where each card landed.

Both validate every card ID via cardsInfo before mutating: AnkiConnect's
forgetCards returns null and setDueDate returns true even for IDs that do
not exist, so a typo would otherwise look like a successful reset. The
shared check lives in card-validation.utils.ts.

Neither action needed a read-only mode change — both were already treated
as scheduling operations rather than content writes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: address review feedback on scheduling tools

setDueDate: idempotentHint false. A range spec like "3-7" re-rolls on
every call, so the same arguments can land cards on different days. The
hint describes the tool rather than one set of arguments, and a client
that auto-retried on it would silently reshuffle scheduling.

Both tools: drop findCards from the cards parameter description. It is an
internal AnkiConnect action, not an exposed MCP tool, so an LLM following
the hint would call something that does not exist. Point at get_cards,
get_due_cards and notesInfo instead.

setDueDate: isolate the post-mutation read-back in its own try/catch. It
shared a try with setDueDate, so an Anki hiccup after the reschedule had
committed was reported as a failed call — inviting a retry, which on a
range spec re-rolls the dates and turns a reporting problem into a
scheduling one. A failed read-back now returns success with an empty
scheduled array and a message saying not to retry.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.content:
ci: lockfile-free pack smoke test; fix(http): honour PORT/HOST/ANKI_CONNECT_URL env vars (#59)

* ci: smoke-test the packed tarball with a lockfile-free install

Follow-up to #56 / #57. CI validated the dependency tree from
package-lock.json, which consumers never receive; a resolution that
only breaks outside the lockfile (like the mixed @nestjs/* pinning in
#56) passed every check and crashed at require-time for every npm user.

Adds scripts/smoke-test-pack.sh (npm run smoke:pack) and a
pack-smoke-test CI job: `npm pack`, install the tarball into a temp
prefix with no lockfile, boot the real `ankimcp --stdio` bin and assert
on the initialize and tools/list responses; also boot the HTTP entry
point under a bounded timeout to validate its require graph.

Suggested by @sudoleg in #56.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01JLHUqkptmARkLmNPhXXTLN

* fix(http): honour PORT, HOST and ANKI_CONNECT_URL env vars in HTTP mode

Commander declared defaults for --port, --host and --anki-connect, so
the parsed options were never undefined and buildConfigInput() let them
override the environment unconditionally. main-http.ts also listened on
the raw CLI values instead of the validated config. Result: in HTTP
mode `PORT=39218 ankimcp` bound 127.0.0.1:3000 and
`ANKI_CONNECT_URL=...` was silently replaced by localhost:8765, despite
both being documented. STDIO and tunnel mode were unaffected (they
never routed through the defaulted options).

- Drop the Commander defaults; the Zod schema is the single owner of
  defaults. Precedence is now CLI flag > env var > default.
- main-http.ts listens on validatedConfig.port/host and the banner
  prints the resolved values via a dedicated BannerOptions type.
- RawCliOptions models what Commander actually returns (strings).
- Blank PORT/HOST env values fall back to the defaults instead of
  failing validation or binding all interfaces.
- Precedence tests for PORT/HOST/ANKI_CONNECT_URL; README rows for
  PORT/HOST and --help text synced.

Surfaced while reviewing the pack smoke test, whose HTTP check tried to
use PORT= and silently bound :3000.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01JLHUqkptmARkLmNPhXXTLN

* fix(config): honour -a in tunnel mode; blank env vars fall back to defaults

- `ankimcp --tunnel -a <url>` was ignored: handleTunnel never forwarded
  ankiConnect into loadValidatedConfig / AppModule.forTunnel. Threaded
  through; tunnel startup now prints the resolved AnkiConnect URL.
- ANKI_CONNECT_URL="", TUNNEL_SERVER_URL="", ANKI_CONNECT_TIMEOUT="" and
  ANKI_CONNECT_API_VERSION="" hard-failed validation instead of falling
  back to their defaults; apply the same blank-to-undefined preprocess
  already used for PORT/HOST.
- An explicit `-a ""` flag is rejected with a usage error (HTTP, tunnel
  and stdio parsers) rather than silently resolving to the default,

entry.title: fix(deps): float the whole @nestjs/* set together (v0.24.2) (#57)
entry.content:
fix(deps): float the whole @nestjs/* set together (v0.24.2) (#57)

Fixes #56.

@nestjs/core was exact-pinned at 11.1.29 while @nestjs/common,
@nestjs/microservices and @nestjs/platform-express floated on
^11.1.29. Nest packages depend on each other's internal modules, so
every fresh `npm i` / `npx` install resolved microservices to 11.2.3,
which requires `@nestjs/core/helpers/safe-instance-decorator` (only in
core >= 11.2.2), and the server died at require-time with
MODULE_NOT_FOUND before any transport opened. CI never saw it because
`npm ci` honours the repo lockfile, which consumers never receive.

All @nestjs/* runtime deps now share the same `^11.1.29` range and move
as a set (lockfile re-resolved to 11.2.3). Verified with a lockfile-free
`npm pack` + install into a temp prefix: stdio boots and answers
`initialize`.

Thanks to @sudoleg for the precise report, root-cause analysis and
verification.

entry.title: fix(deps): migrate to mcp-nest v2 + MCP SDK v2 — emit JSON Schema 202…
entry.content:
fix(deps): migrate to mcp-nest v2 + MCP SDK v2 — emit JSON Schema 2020-12 (v0.24.0) (#54)

* fix(deps): migrate to mcp-nest v2 + MCP SDK v2 — emit JSON Schema 2020-12 (v0.24.0)

Claude Desktop's Code tab rejects every tool call:

    Tool 'listDecks' has an invalid outputSchema: JSON Schema declares an
    unsupported dialect ("$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#").
    The default validator supports JSON Schema 2020-12 only

SEP-1613 made 2020-12 the default dialect, but @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.x
hardcodes draft-07 for input/outputSchema with no opt-out — server/mcp.js calls
the converter with a fixed options object and never passes a target. The
upstream fixes for the 1.x line (typescript-sdk#2085, #2653) have not landed,
so no configuration change in this repo could resolve it. Moving to the v2 SDK,
which mcp-nest v2 requires, removes the cause.

All 96 tool schemas (48 input + 48 output) now emit
https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema.

Fixes #53

mcp-nest 1.9.11 -> 2.0.0 is a re-platform:

- McpModule.forRoot() -> McpStrategy, a NestJS microservice
  CustomTransportStrategy. Each entry point builds one strategy and hands the
  same instance to both AppModule.forX() (as MCP_STRATEGY) and the microservice
  connection.
- 51 capability classes: @Injectable() -> @McpController(), handler params take
  @Payload(). Registered in each primitive module's controllers array;
  AppModule no longer re-lists them (that would instantiate every class twice).
- @modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.30.0 -> @modelcontextprotocol/{core,node,server},
  pinned exactly per prior pin discipline.
- Tunnel mode rebuilt on the public McpTransport interface. TunnelMcpService is
  gone along with its reach into mcp-nest internals: the module-id lookup, a
  copied private buildMcpCapabilities(), and
  registerRequestHandlers(server, {} as any). All three collapse into
  ctx.createBoundServer(session).
- HTTP mode owns its route via McpHttpControllerFor(transport) with
  mount: false. A self-mounted transport route registers on the Express adapter
  outside the Nest pipeline, which would silently bypass the Origin/Host guards.
- OAuth moved to a separate package upstream, so @nestjs/jwt, @nestjs/passport,
  passport, passport-jwt and jsonwebtoken are dropped — they were carried only
  as v1 peer deps and were never imported.

Also fixed, found while reviewing the migration:

- Tunnel cross-client response mix-up. Responses were correlated by the
  client-chosen JSON-RPC id, so two callers using id:1 collided: one received
  the other's payload, the other hung the full 25s timeout. A stale timer's
  unconditional delete could evict a third request, cascading. The transport
  now renumbers internally and restores the caller's id on the way out. The id
  must be a string — the SDK numbers server-initiated requests from 0 through
  the same send() path.
- Removed the env://{name} resource, which returned any environment variable
  verbatim with no allowlist. Over tunnel or --ngrok that exposed the process
  environment to a remote client; under MCPB it handed the model the
  ANKI_CONNECT_API_KEY that manifest.json injects. system://info is kept.
- MCP server identity now comes from validated config instead of direct
  process.env reads, so all three modes advertise the real package version
  (STDIO/HTTP previously reported 1.0.0 while tunnel reported the true one).
- Demoted NestJS RoutesResolver logs to debug. @McpController composes
  @Controller, so all 51 capability classes were announced at startup despite
  exposing no HTTP routes. RouterExplorer stays at info — those three lines are
  the real record of the MCP endpoint.

E2E harness adapted for MCP Inspector v2, which is pinned to 2.2.0 with a
nightly canary tracking latest. Two v2 CLI breaks: server args after the target
are dropped without a `--` separator (so --read-only never reached the server,
making the read-only suite a false negative), and a tool returning isError now
exits 5 after printing the result.

Verified: 75 suites / 1320 unit tests, e2e green, MCPB bundle confirmed working
in Claude Desktop's Code tab, tunnel confirmed working.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01H5PpmrhpkSqs2LGdTBadjf

* docs+test: changelog for v0.24.0, make three orphaned E2E specs reachable

CHANGELOG entry for 0.24.0 — the #53 dialect fix, the mcp-nest v2 re-platform,
the env://{name} removal, the tunnel id-collision fix, and the dropped
passport/JWT peer deps.

E2E is split by filename:

    e2e:test:http   --testPathPatterns='http\.e2e-spec'
    e2e:test:stdio  --testPathPatterns='stdio\.e2e-spec'

and scripts/e2e-full.sh plus all three workflows call only those two.
stats-tools, get-due-cards and add-notes were named *.e2e-spec.ts, matching
neither pattern, so they have never run in any workflow or in CI despite
jest-e2e.config.js collecting them. All three call setTransport("stdio") —
they are stdio specs that missed the naming convention. Renamed so they
actually execute.

stats-tools then needed one fix: it asserted callTool throws on a validation
error, while its HTTP twin asserts the opposite and passes. mcp-nest v2 returns
validation failures as an isError payload from the transport-agnostic strategy,
so both transports emit the same thing; the stdio spec was stale. Confirmed
live against both transports:

    Invalid parameters: [start_date]: Must be ISO date format: YYYY-MM-DD

Its beforeAll timeout also went 60s -> 180s: that fixture is 42 inspector
spawns and each one boots a fresh server in stdio mode, where the http twin
reuses one running server and still needed 90s.

get-due-cards and add-notes were audited field-by-field against the current
tool schemas (including the 0.18.0 and 0.23.0 changes) and needed no edits.
No product bugs surfaced.

Also documents why engines.node stays at >=22.12.0 while the E2E tooling needs
>=22.19.0: the inspector is a devDependency, so consumers must not be forced
higher for a tool they never install.

entry.title: fix(security): harden media-URL SSRF guard against IPv6 transition by…
entry.content:
fix(security): harden media-URL SSRF guard against IPv6 transition bypass (v0.22.5) (#46)

* fix(security): harden media-URL SSRF guard against IPv6 transition bypass

Switch validateMediaUrl() from a range blocklist to a fail-closed
allowlist (only ipaddr.js "unicast" is permitted). The blocklist missed
the IPv6 transition ranges ipaddr.js can return (rfc6052/NAT64,
rfc6145/SIIT, 6to4, teredo, benchmarking, amt), letting an attacker
reach internal targets via a literal like
http://[64:ff9b::169.254.169.254]/ that encodes a private IPv4.
The allowlist closes the entire class, including any range future
ipaddr.js versions add. (GHSA-5286-6cm5-w3qv)

Also hardened, beyond the reported CVE:
- Extract embedded IPv4 from IPv4-mapped (::ffff:0:0/96) AND deprecated
  IPv4-compatible (::/96) IPv6 before the range check, so an internal
  IPv4 wrapped in IPv6 (e.g. ::a9fe:a9fe) cannot bypass the guard.
- Validate ALL resolved DNS records, not just the first, so a host with
  a public record and a private sibling is rejected.
- allowedHosts matching normalizes IPs (embedded-IPv4 + IPv6 form) and
  handles bracketed IPv6 literals; the IP escape hatch requires every
  resolved address to be allowlisted.

Adds 12 tests covering the transition ranges, embedded-IPv4 forms,
multi-record resolution, and allowlist normalization (127 total, green).

Reported by tonghuaroot.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore(release): v0.22.5
